questions.explanation: "yesterday" is a finished past time, so we use the simple past. "go" is irregular: go becomes went, not the regular "goed". "go" and "goes" are present forms, which cannot describe yesterday.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Have you ___ eaten couscous with fish?"
questions.explanation: "Have you ever eaten…?" asks about an experience at any time in your life, so it takes the present perfect with "ever" between the subject and the past participle. "ago", "yesterday" and "last week" point to a finished time, and a finished time never goes with the present perfect.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Last Saturday at three o'clock, my sister ___ a cake for the family."
questions.explanation: At three o'clock last Saturday the action was in progress, so we use the past progressive: was/were + verb + ing. "my sister" is one person (she), so it is "was making". "were making" is for you, we and they; "was make" forgets the -ing; "is making" is present.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative: "He ___ the test last Monday."
questions.explanation: "last Monday" is a finished time, so we use the simple past, and its negative is didn't + base verb: he didn't pass. "didn't passed" marks the past twice; "wasn't pass" uses "be" instead of "did"; "hasn't passed" is the present perfect, which never goes with a finished time.

questions.prompt: Complete: "I ___ my homework, so I can play now."
questions.explanation: The action is very recent and matters now (I can play), so we use the present perfect with "just": have + just + past participle. "I" takes "have", not "has", and the participle of "finish" is "finished", not the base form "finish" or the -ing form "finishing".

options.text: Did they go to Djerba last summer?
Did they went to Djerba last summer?
Have they gone to Djerba last summer?
Were they go to Djerba last summer?

questions.explanation: "last summer" is a finished time, so we use the simple past, and a simple past question is Did + subject + base verb: Did they go? After "did" the verb never takes its past form ("went"); "Have they gone" is the present perfect, impossible with "last summer"; "Were they go" uses "be" instead of "did".
